rv.q: The songs in "Little Shop" are so wittily crafted that they really can be enjoyed several times over.
Porchlight’s Little Shop of Horrors captures the camp, fun, and liveliness of the musical.
It's a gorgeous, wickedly fun night of theatre that also makes a quiet, powerful statement about who gets to stand at the center of the story.
If it’s been a while, or you’ve never seen a stage production of “Little Shop”, it would be hard to beat Porchlight’s production without boarding a flight to New York.
As always with Porchlight, the voices are strong and the instrumentation perfectly balanced under the baton of music director David Fiorello.
Porchlight's Little Shop of Horrors serves as an enjoyable reminder of why the musical has remained a favorite for more than four decades.
Little Shop of Horrors is a fun and campy show and Porchlight’s production captures all that you love about the musical!
The production values are extravagant, strong and relevant.

cn.t: Critics largely praise Porchlight's *Little Shop of Horrors* for its energetic cast and Ashman/Menken's irresistible score, with some noting the staging plays it safe. Still, the campy crowd-pleaser delivers the kitschy joy fans expect.
